standard.title: First Nations media arts and Country/Place
standard.description: explore how First Nations Australians use media arts to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Country/Place
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify media arts works produced by First Nations Australians and describe how visual, audio and interactive elements communicate cultural knowledge. They have not yet explored specifically how media arts communicates connection to and responsibility for Country/Place.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how First Nations Australians use media arts to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Country/Place.

nodes.label: Connection to Country/Place in media arts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how a First Nations Australian media arts work communicates connection to and responsibility for Country/Place — naming at least one specific media arts concept used (framing, language, sound, symbols).
nodes.minimum_width: Explore one First Nations Australian media arts work that communicates connection to Country/Place and identify at least one media arts concept (framing, language, symbols, sound) used to communicate that connection.
nodes.typical_width: Explore First Nations Australian media arts works across forms that communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place — identifying how cultural expressions include: naming Country and Traditional Owners, acknowledging Ancestors, singing/speaking in language, communicating knowledge about seasons, land, sea, sky and waterways; recognise how screen-based storytelling maintains language and ways of life.
wider: Explore First Nations Australian media arts works created for ceremonial or festival contexts — collecting and reflecting on how the occasion, purpose and media arts choices communicate knowledge about Country/Place

Investigate how First Nations Australian media artists use screen-based storytelling to maintain language and unique ways of life — examining specific examples and discussing what would be at risk if these works were not made
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding the specific connection between First Nations Australian media arts and Country/Place is the conceptual foundation for this standard — without it, exploration of specific elements and practices has no cultural grounding.

response_modes.reason: Students need guided inquiry with community resources or accredited materials to connect observable media elements to their Country/Place significance — this is not interpretable from the text or images alone.

success_criteria: Student can identify how a First Nations Australian media arts work communicates connection to Country/Place
Student can name at least one media arts concept (framing, language, sound, symbols) used to communicate that connection

nodes.label: Diversity of First Nations media arts expression
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare how different First Nations Australian media arts works communicate connection to Country/Place — noting how different media arts concepts, languages and purposes produce different works.
nodes.minimum_width: Explore two different First Nations Australian media arts works communicating connection to Country/Place and describe one similarity and one difference in how they use media arts concepts.
nodes.typical_width: Collect and share information about First Nations Australian media arts works created for different occasions and purposes; compare how different media arts concepts (languages, symbols, icons) and forms communicate connection to Country/Place; explore the diversity of First Nations Australian cultures through media arts works.
wider: Explore an interactive map of First Nations Australian languages as a media arts work — investigating how media technologies and languages create a relationship with the viewer, and discussing how digital tools communicate the diversity of First Nations cultures

Compare how two First Nations Australian communities use media arts to communicate their distinct relationships to Country/Place — identifying what is shared and what is specific to each community's culture and story

response_modes.reason: Expose students to multiple First Nations Australian media arts works from different communities, forms and occasions — diversity is the point, not a single representative example.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The diversity of First Nations Australian media arts works (ceremonial, language preservation, interactive digital, stop motion, animation) communicating Country/Place is genuinely rich — students who explore across multiple works develop a much more accurate and respectful understanding.
success_criteria: Student can compare at least two First Nations Australian media arts works communicating connection to Country/Place
Student can describe at least one way each work uses media arts concepts differently, and explain what that difference communicates
